competitive_landscape: WETA's diesel fleet is both the incumbent and the decarbonization partner; Golden Gate Ferry runs the Marin services; BART is the rail substitute. A fast, zero-emission foiling tier complements rather than competes — it serves WETA's own mandate and opens OD pairs the displacement fleet cannot. Uber's Bay Area home market is the demand-platform partner.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the entire bay network — every commuter and tech-campus hop (SF, Oakland, Alameda, Marin, Peninsula, Vallejo) is comfortably in all-electric range, matching WETA's decarbonization mandate exactly.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR is not required for the bay; available for any future Sacramento-River-Delta or open-coast extension.

precedents.why_it_matters: Shows public authorities adopting zero-emission fast vessels to meet decarbonization mandates — WETA's exact situation.

regulatory_note: US Coast Guard Subchapter T inspection; WETA / public-transit procurement and terminal access are the gating processes; California CEQA review applies, and a zero-emission, low-wake profile aligns directly with CARB and Bay Area air-quality goals.
seasonality: Year-round commuter demand; summer afternoon wind and chop on the exposed central bay require operating discipline, which a foiling hull handles better than a small displacement craft.

summary: San Francisco Bay is the strongest US public-transit case Navier has: the San Francisco Bay Ferry (operated by WETA, the Water Emergency Transportation Authority) already runs a multi-terminal scheduled network, the bridges are chronic chokepoints, and the tech-commuter base across SF, Oakland, the Peninsula and Marin is dense and premium. Every bay hop sits comfortably inside Pioneer II all-electric range, and WETA has a public mandate to decarbonize its diesel fleet — a clean, fast, zero-emission foiling tier slots directly into that mandate while opening new origin-destination pairs (Peninsula tech campuses, Oyster Point biotech) that today's displacement ferries serve too slowly. The Bay Area pairs with Hawaii and Florida as the third US demand cluster in the Uber USA story.
tagline: The most credible US public-transit water market — an established ferry authority, chronic bridge congestion, and a dense tech-commuter base around one sheltered bay.
